Until then an orchestrator that carries the owner's verdict on a goal writes it as a note_day with kind proposal, and the owner runs goal review. goal add and the chapter commands stay off the door: what the owner is for, and what a stretch of their life is called, are said at home.

docs.title: Derived material follows the policy
docs.text:
A draft follows the policy, not the head. This is draft/v1 rule 7 and ADR 0016's paragraph of that name, written by fix/derived-invalidation-on-policy (#273) while this amendment was open; the amendment takes them as they stand, with their names, and adds to them. A writer that reads under a crossing entry records the entry's version under extra.policy_version: the SHA-256, lowercase hex, of the RFC 8785 JSON of the entry's {"max_tier", "model", "until"} (null for one it does not set), so the same three values are the same version however the file spells them and whatever else the entry says (docs/dream.md, When the entry changes). There is no second field. A reader shows a draft only while that entry, as it counts today, allows the draft's tier: its max_tier today, and 0 past its until or with the entry removed, never the ceiling the draft was read under. An owner who lowers an entry, or lets it lapse, has lowered it for every draft already written. A draft above it is withheld whatever the head: the reader that holds the record says so in one row, superseded by policy and why (draft_withheld in JSON), and shows nothing of the text; the line stays in the record; doctor names the days; and dream --catch-up dreams such a day again under the entry as it is, superseding the draft, as it does a day whose draft was dreamed under another version. A draft that names no version, every one written before #273, is held to the entry by its tier alone.

Amendment 1 adds two things. The rule holds for a draft of every unit: a person draft is withheld on the person page as a day's is on the Day, with the same row. And a reader through a crossing MUST hold a draft to that crossing's own ceiling as well, as it counts at the moment the reader serves (ADR 0022 rule 6). Hidden there is what a line above the ceiling is: the draft is left out of the unit's page through that crossing, with no row, its line is left out of the day's lines and counted where the crossing counts what it holds back (above_ceiling through the door, counts.held_back in the crossing package's manifest), and nothing of it crosses, not its id and not its evidence. Both hold for every crossing a draft can reach: the mcp door, the crossing package, the shared page, the trip bundle, the vault and the site. The owner reading at home crosses nothing, so at home the entry alone holds a draft back, and the page says so.

For example, the draft of 13 June on the draft/v1 page is tier 2, dreamed under a dream entry of {"max_tier": 2}. With the mcp entry at {"max_tier": 2} the door's day tool shows it; with the mcp entry lowered to {"max_tier": 1}, the same call answers with no draft and day_lines counts the draft line in above_ceiling, with no line written and no draft re-dreamed, and day at home shows the draft as before. Lower the dream entry to {"max_tier": 1} instead, and the door holds the draft back and counts it the same way, while day at home prints superseded by policy: tier 2, above max_tier 1 of the 'dream' entry and why, in place of the draft and with nothing of its text; dream --catch-up then dreams the day again under the entry as it is.

What does not change: the envelope, the four profiles' other fields, the tier rule, the page digest of a signed day, and the hash of every line already written. The four profiles are, with this amendment, still new and not frozen: their schemas may change while this RFC is a draft, and each becomes frozen only by RFC 0031's process.

docs.title: Amendment 2 — days together reach the relationship reader
docs.text:
Dated 2026-10-18, the owner's decision (open question 1 of the relationship reader's slice 1, #328). Amendment 1 kept "a stay they were found at" out of a person's set, because the with module's days together rest on location lines. The owner wants them in: time spent together is most of what passes between two people, and a reader that sees only the chat does not know it. A person's set for people ask and dream person now adds the days together in the window: each day the with module counts as a day together (its confirmed set, docs/people.md: an attendee of a timed entry held at the owner's stay, a speaker of a recording made there, a note written there that says "with "), with its date, the named place of each stay they shared, the places.json name only (a stay at no named place says a place with no name, never coordinates, never "near" a place), and the line ids it rests on as its evidence, so a sentence about time together cites them and a reader resolves the citation against them. Nothing else of the stay crosses: no coordinate, no location line, and no words of a line it rests on that is not a line of the set (a note's day, not its text).

The gate is every other line's: a day together counts only on the lines of it at or under the relationship entry's max_tier, on days the owner has signed unless the entry lifts that (include_unsigned), and nothing at all without the entry or after its until. A day whose every line the gate refuses is not sent and is counted as held back. Each day goes as references (L…) like the other lines, a line already in the set keeping its reference, never an id; the answer's JSON counts them (days_together: {sent, held_back}), and a person draft keeps the number under extra.days_together. The prompts that say so are relationship-ask/2 and dream-person/2. read_count stays the size of the set, the lines; a line a day together rests on counts toward the draft's tier as any line read does.

What does not change: the envelope, draft/v1, the five channels of the set, the store's files (a day together is read again from the record each time, never kept in the store), and every line already written.

19 October 2026, the owner's answer to #332's open question: a day together's place name takes the tier of what it rests on, the highest tier of the owner's location lines behind the stay and of the line that names the company, so a day whose stay rests on location lines above the entry's max_tier is not sent and is counted as held back, never its name alone.

docs.title: Relation to RFC 0037
docs.text:
RFC 0037 (entities, a draft at this writing) was written before this RFC merged and cites nothing from it; the cross-reference is made here, from the side that merged first (amendment 1).

  • goal/v1 and review/v1 are the general status pattern. Something the owner holds, said once in a line of its own, and the owner's verdict on it at a date, in another line that a later verdict stands over; anything may propose, only the owner disposes, and every line is source manual. RFC 0037's status/v1 specialises that pattern for orgs and ideas: its entity is what a review's goal is, its dispositions (six for an org, five for an idea) are the kind's own words where a goal has advancing, stalled, done, let go and superseded, and its proposal keeps a draft's proposal beside the owner's answer. One difference is for the comment period of either RFC: a late verdict here is dated by its at, with recorded_at saying when it was written, and a late status there by since. 0037's open question 11 asks which RFC specifies the goal review: this one, review/v1. A goal is not a sixth kind of status/v1, and RFC 0034's four dispositions are a commitment's, not a goal's.
  • review KIND is one loop. A proposal, the owner's answer as a line, and the next proposal only when the record moves: that is 0037's review sitting for identities and statuses, and it is this RFC's for goals. When 0037 lands, review goal MAY be one more kind of the sitting, listing the standing open goals with no review in their current period, and answering through the writer goal review uses: one writer, not two.

docs.title: What this changes in SPEC, when adopted
docs.text:
Nothing in §2–3. In §1, logbook.json gains day_start as an optional key, with the rule above. In §3.2, the sentence on the record's zone gains the day's boundary, and §3.2.1 and §3.2.7 gain the four items above. The four profiles join the §4 table (tier 2, MUST, for three; the highest tier of its evidence for draft/v1) and the draft list of rfcs/README.md. ADR 0016's file gains the key signed_within_days, and RFC 0034 rule 5 gains the sentence that the entry's rule applies where the command's default does not. Each profile freezes by RFC 0031's process, with a fixture under conformance/profiles/, once a second reader exists.

Amendment 1 changes nothing in SPEC: the person unit and window are draft/v1's own, extra.policy_version is rule 7's, and the hiding rule is ADR 0016's ceiling applied to a derived line, as ADR 0016's paragraph Derived material follows the policy, not the head already has it. ADR 0022's list of write tools is unchanged.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Why one line per goal and a new line to reword. The log is not edited (SPEC §3), and a goal reworded is a decision in itself: the owner wanted something else, or wanted to say it better, and the record keeps both. supersedes is the mechanism every edited thing in the record already uses (RFC 0010 rule 2, RFC 0034 rule 3).
  • Why a review is on the date it is about. at is when the thing happened (SPEC §2), and the thing is the verdict on a stretch that ended then. The record's own recorded_at says when it was written; a second field would say the same twice.
  • Why a draft names the head and the count it read. A draft is a reading of the record at a moment. The head says which record it read; the count says how much of the unit, so a reader can tell a draft written from four lines from one written from forty, and a draft written under a ceiling of 1 from one written on the home machine. When the unit grows, the standing draft is of a smaller unit than the page now shows, and a reader can say so.
  • Why every segment has evidence or a mark. A model's sentence with no line behind it is the one kind of content the record has never held: not observed, not the owner's. It is allowed in, because the owner wants to read it, on the one condition that it never looks like the rest.
  • Why the draft's tier is what it read, not what it cited. A tier is what a line may give away. A model that read a tier-3 line may have been shaped by it in a sentence that cites a tier-1 line, and no reader can tell. The ceiling the model read under is the only bound that holds.
  • Why day_start is a setting and not a line. It is the owner's habit, not an event; it has no at. It belongs with timezone, which is the same kind of thing: how the owner's clock maps onto the record's instants. And logbook.json already requires writers to preserve keys they do not know (SPEC §1), so a record that sets it is read by an old writer without losing it.
  • Why refuse rather than guess. A reader that groups by calendar day on a record whose owner set 06:00 would sign, cross and digest the wrong days, silently. SPEC §2 made the same choice for an unknown zone.
  • Why the window is on the signature's day and not the day signed. The point is how recently the owner looked. A rule on the gap between a day and its signature would make a day whose page grew after N days uncrossable for good, since no later signature could close the gap; a rule on the signature's recency is refreshed by signing again, which is what RFC 0034 asks the owner to do when a page changes.
  • Why --unsigned does not lift it. --unsigned is the owner at the console lifting the command's default for one run. A policy key is a ceiling (ADR 0016): the command cannot exceed it, which is what makes an unattended destination safe to give a fixed command line.
  • Why a person's set is contact and not mention (amendment 1). "What matters to Ola lately" is a question about what passed between the owner and Ola, and the lines where Ola is on the other end are that. A mention is someone's word about Ola, often a third person's, and finding one takes a match on text that no two implementations would make alike; the five channels are found by refs and resolution lines, the same way everywhere. And a model asked about one person that may read every note naming them has, in practice, read the record.
  • Why the window is on the line (amendment 1). A day draft's unit bounds itself; a person does not, and "lately" means a different stretch on each run. Without the window a reader could not tell a draft of three weeks from one of three years, nor check that the evidence is in the set.
  • Why the writers are commands and not tools (amendment 1). A goal, a verdict and a chapter are the owner's words, tier 2, and the door's ceiling is usually 1: an orchestrator could write a goal it cannot read back. sign_day went through the door because the owner's reading of a page happens where the page is shown; a verdict on a goal can follow the same road when the owner wants it to, by name, and not before.
  • Why the ceiling that counts is today's (amendment 1). A ceiling is the owner's statement of what a destination may see now (ADR 0016). A draft is derived, and derived material that kept the ceiling it was made under would be the one thing in the record a lowered ceiling did not reach. Hiding costs nothing: the line is still in the record, and raising the ceiling again shows it.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Should the signed day's page name the boundary? RFC 0034's page digest is over day, tz and the line hashes. A record that changes day_start makes every signature read as not matching, which is correct and loud, but a reader cannot tell a page that changed because a line was appended from one that changed because the boundary moved. Adding day_start to the pre-image is one field; it is also a change to a profile that is already in the conformance sample. Left for RFC 0034's own amendment.
  2. What writes a draft. This RFC fixes the line and not the writer. note_day through the door writes a note/v1 with labels: ["proposal"] today (docs/mcp.md); whether a draft_day tool joins write, or a command on the home machine runs the model, is the agent layer's to decide, under ADR 0022. (Since answered for the day: dream day, docs/dream.md, runs the model on the home machine under the dream entry. Amendment 1 adds the person unit and its input set, and leaves its writer open; it names the writers of goals, reviews and chapters, none of them a door tool yet.)
  3. A star on a draft. "A star" here is a keeper/v1 line, the one mark the owner makes today, and it marks a photo. A mark on a draft segment, "this sentence is right", does not exist and is not invented here; the owner confirms a segment by confirming the lines it rests on, in a signed day.
  4. Overlapping chapters. The rule on the chapter page is that chapters do not overlap and a writer refuses one that would; a reader that meets two standing chapters open on one day shows the later by from, then seq, and marks the clash. Whether an owner wants nested stretches (a passage inside a sabbatical) is not decided.
  5. A review of nothing. A review names a goal. A verdict on a period with no goal behind it, "the quarter went badly", is a note today, and stays one.
  6. period and at. The period is the stretch that ends on, or holds, the review's at; which of the two is left to the writer and the owner's habit (a week reviewed on its Sunday, a month on its last day or its first). A reader shows the period as written and derives nothing from it.

docs.title: RFC 0037 — Entities: orgs, ideas, places and assets reviewed like people
docs.text:
Status: draft · 2026-10-13 · comment period closed 2026-10-14: the owner decided its twelve questions, and each decision is in the body (§16, Decided) · amended 2026-10-14: an org's status reason stays on its tier-3 line, never a note/v1 (§8, §10.2, §10.5) · amended 2026-10-15: an org's portfolio is an optional field of its tier-3 status line, never an entity/v1 line (§8, §9, §10.2, §11) · amended 2026-10-16: a database row is its own root, and is proposed as an idea only when its Type says Idea (§4.3, §4.6) · amends RFC 0035 (its amendment 1) and ADR 0018 rule 4

The record knows five kinds of thing that recur across its lines and that the owner wants a page for: a person, an org (a company invested in or passed on, a club, a brand), a place, an asset (a boat, an aircraft, a car) and an idea (a thread that starts as a repository README, continues in Notion, is spoken of in transcripts, and is built or killed). People review (RFC 0035, docs/people.md#review) settled the mechanism for one of them: observed references resolve to a canonical entity under the owner's control; an unresolved proposal is not an identity; nothing is promoted on its own. This RFC generalises that mechanism to the other four, so that one review sitting (review KIND) and one page pattern serve all five, and adds the one thing the other four need that a person does not: a status, as lines, proposed by the dream and disposed by the owner. A person has no status. A goal is not an entity and has its own verdict, RFC 0036's review/v1; a promise has RFC 0034's dispositions (§12).

Three payload profiles are proposed, entity/v1, entity-review/v1 and status/v1, all new and none of them one of the RFC 0031 freezes: their schemas may change while this RFC is a draft, and they become frozen only by RFC 0031's process. The envelope does not change: no spec version bump, no new conformance fixture, no new ADR. There is one road per kind: a person binds through resolution/v1 (RFC 0006, frozen), and nothing about the canonical person of RFC 0006 and RFC 0035 changes; an org, an idea, a place and an asset bind through entity/v1 only (§3.3). The owner's no, for every kind, is one profile, entity-review/v1 (§6). This RFC amends two documents in place, each with a dated section and no rewrite: RFC 0035, whose no is written as entity-review/v1 from now on (its amendment 1), and ADR 0018 rule 4, whose registry entries are never deleted and are closed by a status line (the amendment).

RFC 0036 (goals, reviews, drafts and chapters) merged while this RFC was in comment, and this RFC was written before it. It is cited by number wherever this RFC speaks of a draft, a review or a writer: what the dream writes is a draft/v1 line (RFC 0036), and a draft is a proposal, never a fact; a goal's verdict is a review/v1 line (RFC 0036), which status/v1 is not; and the writers of §5 and §10 hold the writer lock as day sign does (RFC 0034 amendment 3), as RFC 0036 amendment 1 (open at this writing, #269) has its goal, review and chapter writers do.

docs.title: 1. Words
docs.text:
• An entity is a canonical thing of one kind, person, org, place, asset or idea, identified in this record by { type, id, registry } as RFC 0006 mints them. It exists because a line names it: a resolution/v1 line for a person, an entity/v1 line for the other four (or, for an org, a company resolution line of RFC 0006 written before this RFC, §3.3).
  • An observed entity is what one source saw, keyed by its strongest identifier for its kind (§4), and nobody chose it. It is a row of a derived table in the index, never a line.
  • A ref is a source-native identifier, { kind, value }, as RFC 0006 defines it. A ref resolves to an entity or to nothing.
  • A touch is any standing line that resolves, through one of its refs, to the entity: a mail from its domain, a meeting with its people, a Notion page under its root, a stay in its circle, a position report of its hull.
  • A status is the owner's disposition of an org, an idea, a place or an asset at a point in time, one status/v1 line; the current status is the last standing one. A person has none; a goal's verdict is RFC 0036's review/v1.
  • The dream is logbook dream (docs/dream.md): each morning a model reads yesterday and writes one draft/v1 line about it (RFC 0036), and nothing else. With this RFC the dream's run also evaluates the status rules of §10.4 against the head, and the review shows what they propose; a proposal is never a line, and the owner's answer is (RFC 0034: agents draft, the owner signs; RFC 0036: a draft is a proposal until the owner confirms it through an act of their own).

docs.title: 2. Why one mechanism
docs.text:
People review taught the rule that keeps a queue alive: derive an observed identity from the strongest identifier the observation carries, never from the id a source gives one observation, or one person explodes into a row per observation. The same rule applies to a company seen through four roads (its mail domain, its people's calendar invitations, the WhatsApp group with its name, the ledger line that paid it) and to an idea seen through four others (the README of a repository, the Notion page it grew into, the transcript where it was talked through, the task that said "write up the fjord kiosk"). Without a canonical entity, the Manifest shelf is a list of domains and the Ideas shelf a list of page titles. With one, each company and each idea is one thread, with every touch on it, the people in it, the documents that carry it, and what the owner decided about it, and why.

Places (docs/places.md#review) and assets (ADR 0018) already have registries, places.json and assets.json, and places already have a review. They join here so that the sitting is one sitting, the no is one line and the page is one page; their registries stay (§3.3), and a place given up or a boat sold is a status, never a deleted entry (§10.3).

docs.title: 3.1 Line
docs.text: kind MUST be entity. source MUST be manual: an entity exists because the owner said so, through review KIND --accept or --name, setup places review, setup assets add, or logbook add. tier is the highest tier of the evidence it cites (SPEC §4), and is never 3: an entity/v1 line MUST NOT cite a tier-3 line (§8). at is when the owner said so; end is null.

docs.title: 3.2 Payload
docs.text:
Field Type Req Meaning schema "entity/v1" MUST entity object MUST { type, id, registry }. type is one of org, place, asset, idea, never person (§3.3); registry MUST be logbook; id MUST be a UUIDv7 minted in this record (§3.4 rule 4), or the id the registry file already holds for a place or an asset (§3.3). A private or interpreter namespace MUST NOT appear as a registry (ADR 0013.2) label string MUST the name, as the owner gave it or accepted it: Nordmann Verft AS, the fjord kiosk refs array of object SHOULD the identifiers this line binds to the entity, each { kind, value }, of the kinds the entity's type takes (below). A later line for the same entity adds refs; it never removes one (retract the line that bound it) aliases array of string MAY other spellings of the label, for the page's head and for matching: Nordmann Verft, NV keys object MAY the dedupe key of §9 as the writer computed it, for a reader without the table method string MAY owner evidence array of string MAY ids of the lines the entity was seen on when it was accepted; never a tier-3 line supersedes string MAY the id of an earlier entity/v1 line for the same entity this replaces (a relabel) logbook_head hex sha256 MAY the head the proposal was read against extra object MAY what the kind needs and nothing else: an org's country or register number as the owner typed it; an idea's one-line pitch; nothing a line of the record already holds

The ref kinds each type takes. domain is RFC 0006's; the others are this RFC's, each lower-cased and folded as given:

entity.type refs[].kind org domain (the registered domain, §4.2), repo (a code host and an organisation, github.com/nordmann-verft), group (a chat's display name, folded), merchant (a ledger merchant string, folded) idea page (notion:<page id>), repo (a host, an owner and a name, github.com/nordmann-verft/kiosk), title (a title's words, folded and sorted, as RFC 0035's name) place place (the name as places.json spells it) asset mmsi, icao24, registration

An address is never an org's ref: an email ref is a person's, through resolution/v1, and an address's org is found by its registered domain. A ref of a kind its type does not take makes the line invalid.

docs.title: 3.3 One road per kind
docs.text:
Each kind binds its refs through exactly one profile, and a reader looks a ref up through that profile alone:

Kind Binds through Notes person resolution/v1 (RFC 0006, frozen) the alias walk of RFC 0006 rule 6, at most four hops; unchanged org entity/v1 and, read and never written, the company resolution lines of RFC 0006 (below) idea entity/v1 place entity/v1 beside places.json, the setting asset entity/v1 beside assets.json, the setting

There is no resolution/v2, and no profile takes a second road. An entity/v1 line never names a person, and no writer of this RFC writes a resolution/v1 line for anything but a person.

The person. Nothing in RFC 0006 or in how docs/people.md resolves a person changes, and no line is rewritten; the one change is the profile of the owner's no (RFC 0035 amendment 1):

General form The person today an entity exists because a line names it a person exists because a resolution/v1 line names { type: "person", id, registry: "logbook" } (RFC 0006, Minting) its label is the label of the first standing line that names it the same (docs/people.md#who-is-a-person) its refs are every ref whose lookup ends at it every ref whose alias walk (RFC 0006 rule 6) ends at a line naming it review person people review, which it aliases (§5); only the line its --reject writes changes the owner's no entity-review/v1, type person (§6), which people review writes from now on; the people-review/v1 lines already written are read forever (RFC 0035 amendment 1) its page logbook people NAME, which gains the common sections of §7 without losing a row its status none: a person is not disposed of

A person minted by a resolution is complete. Its other spellings are the labels of its resolution lines, as docs/people.md reads them; there is no entity/v1 line for a person to carry them.

Orgs and company. RFC 0006 allows entity.type company in a resolution line, and the profile is frozen, so the value stays where it was written. A standing resolution/v1 line whose entity.type is company is read as an org: its entity.id is the org's id, its label a label of the org, and the ref it binds resolves to the org as if an entity/v1 line of the same at bound it. No such line is rewritten (SPEC §3), and no writer writes a new one: an org's domains, repositories, groups and merchants are bound by its entity/v1 line's refs. A record whose only line for an org is a company resolution has an org with no entity/v1 line, and it is complete; the first review org --accept that matches it writes an entity/v1 line with the same id (§3.4 rule 4). company is a legacy value, read as org and never written, and org is the kind's one word (§16, question 12).

Places. A place keeps its registry: places.json is the setting, read by every reader each run, and renaming a place changes no line (docs/places.md). Its entity id is the place's name, as the file spells it, under registry logbook; a place gets no UUID because a places.json entry has none to carry. An entity/v1 line for a place is written when setup places review --accept (or review place --accept) runs after this RFC is adopted, beside the note/v1 naming line it writes today, and carries { kind: "place", value: "<name>" } and the stay lines as evidence; a place named before has no line and is complete. RFC 0006's place resolution, a stay to a wikidata or osm id, is unchanged and is a different statement: that the named place is a known public place. It binds no canonical place.

Assets. An asset keeps its registry: assets.json, { id, kind, name, mmsi?, icao24?, registration? } (ADR 0018). Its entity id is the registry's id. An entity/v1 line for an asset binds the identifiers the registry already names as refs (mmsi, icao24, registration), so that a line naming the hull without the registry resolves to it; setup assets add writes one. A location/v1 line's subject is the asset's id and needs no resolution.

A registry entry, of either file, is never deleted: a place given up or an asset sold or let go is closed by a status/v1 line with until (§10.3; ADR 0018 rule 4, as amended).

docs.title: 3.4 Rules
docs.text:
1. An entity/v1 line never modifies a line it cites. Readers join by ref.
  2. One road. A ref resolves to at most one person, through resolution/v1, and to at most one entity of each other kind, through the last standing entity/v1 line of that kind that binds it (and, for an org, the company resolution lines read as §3.3 says; a ref bound by both resolves by the later line). A writer refuses to bind a ref that already resolves to another entity of the same kind, and says which.
  3. Retraction (RFC 0003) applies: a retracted entity/v1 line binds nothing, and the refs it bound fall back to whatever other line binds them, or to nothing. Retracting the minting line of an entity with standing status/v1 lines leaves them standing, and the reader shows them under the id with the label the status line carries (§10.2).
  4. Minting. The first entity/v1 line for a new org or idea mints a UUIDv7 as entity.id. A review KIND --accept MUST look the dedupe key (§9) up before minting, in the entity/v1 lines and, for an org, in the company resolution lines, and MUST reuse the id when the key already resolves; the log is the registry, and there is no registry file for orgs or ideas.
  5. Nothing requires the profile. A record with no entity/v1 line is complete; its people are complete as RFC 0006 leaves them, its orgs as their company resolutions leave them, and its places and assets as their files leave them.

docs.title: 4. Observed → canonical, per kind
docs.text:
The observed entities are one derived table in the index, observed_entities in index.sqlite, with a kind column (person, org, idea, place, asset) and one row per (kind, strongest identifier): the display names seen, the identifiers as the lines wrote them, counts per source and per line kind, the days seen, first and last seen, the tier of the evidence, a few line ids, for an org the hint (§4.2), and the canonical entity the row resolves to when one of its identifiers has a line standing as written (RFC 0035's rule: the readers look a ref up as the line carries it). It is built from the standing lines through the index, the owner's own identities left out, stamped with the head and with the digests of places.json, assets.json, policy/stays.json and policy/entities.json (§4.6), served while they stand, rebuilt when the record grows. Its shape is checked with PRAGMA table_info; a table of another shape is built again, never read. Nothing is written to the record.

observed_people and observed_places, the tables of today, become views over observed_entities (kind = 'person', kind = 'place') with the columns they have now, for one release, so a reader or a test of today reads them unchanged; the release after drops them, and its changelog says so. A view's shape is checked as a table's is.

The strongest-identifier rule holds for every kind: an observed entity's identity is derived from the strongest identifier the observation carries, in the order its kind gives, and never from the id a source gives one observation.

docs.title: 4.1 person
docs.text: As RFC 0035 and docs/people.md#review: email, else phone in E.164, else the name's words folded and sorted. Evidence: mail/v1, message/v1, transcript/v1, event/v1. Unchanged.

docs.title: 4.2 org
docs.text:
Strongest identifier, in this order:

  1. the registered domain (the public suffix plus one label: nordmann-verft.example from post.nordmann-verft.example), from a mail/v1 from, to, cc or bcc address, or an event/v1 attendee's email ref, lower-cased. A domain in the public mail providers list (§4.6) names nobody's org and is skipped: example.org is a family's provider in the synthetic record and tells nothing;
  2. else the GitHub org: the first path segment of a browse/v1 url on github.com, or of a link under a task/v1's extra.links, lower-cased (github.com/nordmann-verft); whether it is an organisation or a user's own account the reader cannot always tell, and the hint says what it guesses;
  3. else the group name: a message/v1 whose chat.type is group, by chat.name folded (nordmann verft board); the group is the observation, the people in it are persons and are reviewed as such;
  4. else the merchant: a transaction/v1 merchant string, folded, when the same string recurs on three or more lines (a merchant seen once is noise; the threshold is a hypothesis).

The hint. The kind on every line is org, and only org: a company, a club, a brand and a family's own domain are all orgs if the owner accepts them. What the queue guesses about an observed org is a column of its row, hint, one of company, brand, community or personal, and nothing else:

hint When personal a domain whose every address seen resolves to a canonical person, three of them at most (personal_max_people, §4.6): a family's own domain; or a GitHub path whose segment is a handle ref of a canonical person: their own account community the strongest identifier is a group name brand the strongest identifier is a merchant string company anything else: a domain or a GitHub organisation

The hint ranks the queue and does nothing else: proposals are ranked by score, then by hint in the order company, community, brand, personal, and the row shows it ([personal]). It is never written to a line, never part of a key, and never read by a page or a shelf; the owner's accept writes an org, whatever the hint said.

The proposal: an observed org not yet placed against each canonical org, scored by what speaks for the pair, a plain sum as people review's:

Evidence Points What it means same domain 60 a domain ref of the canonical org (or of a company resolution line read as it) spells the registered domain same GitHub org 50 a repo ref of the canonical org has the same first segment same name 20, +5 per further source up to +10 the display name (a mail's from.name, a group's name, a merchant string, a repo's org) and the label or an alias are one name: the same words in any order, case, punctuation and the forms AS, ASA, Ltd, Inc, GmbH, AB aside; two words at least, or one word of six letters or more the org's people 10 per canonical person, up to 30 a canonical person whose address is at one of this org's domains was seen on the observed lines (an attendee, a sender, a group member) together on the same days 2 per day, up to 20 both were seen on the day; days alone never propose

A domain alone, matching no canonical org, proposes a new org with the domain as its name and the names the sources gave it (the display name of a from is read; a signature in a body is not, because the body is never read), as places review proposes a blank with the names its sources gave.

docs.title: 4.3 idea
docs.text:
Strongest identifier, in this order:

  1. the Notion root page: the sync notion event/v1 line's page id, or the topmost of "the titles above it" when the integration can see that page, as page (notion:<id>). A page under a root is the root's idea unless the owner says otherwise; the lineage is the evidence and the sub-pages are the documents (§7). A database row is its own root: a page that is a row of a Notion database (its lines carry the row's database, or name a database, or a later API's data source, as their parent) is its own idea and is never folded into the page above the database, so an Ideas database gives one idea per row and a page under a row is the row's;
  2. else the repository: a browse/v1 url, a task/v1 link or a sync drive file name of the form owner/name on a code host, as repo (github.com/nordmann-verft/kiosk, lower-cased);
  3. else the title words: a task/v1 title, a transcript/v1 title, or a Notion page title, folded and sorted, as title, when the same folded title recurs on two or more lines of two or more sources. A title seen once in one source is noise. A transcript's summary is never read for a topic: it is the provider's words about the owner's, and the owner names the idea.

A database row is proposed only when its Type select says Idea (idea_rows, §4.6, names another select and option), as the row's latest line holding its properties says it: a row of another type, and a page under one, is never proposed, and a page that is no row is proposed as before.

The proposal, scored:

Evidence Points What it means same page 60 the observed page, or one above it, is a page ref of the canonical idea same repo 50 the same repo ref same title 20, +5 per further source up to +10 the folded title and the label or an alias are one name: the same words in any order, the articles the, a, an aside; one word of six letters or more suffices (kiosk) the idea's people 10 per canonical person, up to 30 a canonical person who was on the idea's lines (a Notion actor, a transcript participant, a task's assignee) was seen on the observed lines the same week 5 per week, up to 20 the observed title was seen in a week the idea was touched

An idea is the owner's own and the dream never mints one: an observed page, repo or title with no canonical idea proposes a new idea named by its title, for the owner to accept, rename or reject. A spark that was never written anywhere is not in the record and is not proposed; logbook add names it.

docs.title: 4.4 place
docs.text: As today (docs/places.md#review): the observed place is a cluster of stays within 75 m, ranked by nights then hours, named by what the sources already said (Timeline visits, calendar locations held during the stay, photo libraries, Dawarich). Nothing is looked up and no coordinate leaves the machine. The strongest identifier is the cluster's centre, rounded to six decimals, written as a point ref (55.600000,4.436000) where a line carries it (§6). review place is setup places review with this RFC's queue shape; the accept and name semantics are the page's, and the reject writes a line (§5, §6).

docs.title: 4.5 asset
docs.text:
An observed asset is one of:

  1. a subject on a location/v1 line (subject set) that assets.json does not name: lines from another machine's registry, or a hull reported under an id the registry never held;
  2. an aircraft registration on a flight/v1 line (aircraft.registration) seen on three or more flights, or on a keeper/v1 boarding pass that names a tail; the owner's own aircraft flies its owner more than once, an airline's does not;
  3. an MMSI or callsign named in the extra of an AIS report of a vessel that the registry does not know, when it recurs across days near the owner's own hull (a raft-up neighbour, a club boat).

Strongest identifier: mmsi, else icao24, else registration, else the subject id. The proposal matches on the same identifier (60), the same registration spelled two ways (ZZ-ABC and ZZABC, 50), or the same name on the report and in the registry (20). Accepting writes the asset into assets.json as setup assets add does, and an entity/v1 line binding the identifiers. Nothing is synced for a new asset until the owner asks (ADR 0018: the record records what was asked for). An entry closed by a status line (§10.3) is still in the registry and still names its subject: its lines are never proposed as a new asset.

docs.title: 4.6 policy/entities.json
docs.text:
One setting, read each run, never a line:

{"public_mail_providers": ["gmail.com", "outlook.com", "hotmail.com", "icloud.com", "me.com", "proton.me", "yahoo.com", "example.org"],
 "merchant_min_lines": 3, "title_min_lines": 2, "personal_max_people": 3,
 "code_hosts": ["github.com", "gitlab.com", "codeberg.org"],
 "mute_days": 365, "stale_after_days": {"hold": 1095, "exploring": 730},
 "idea_rows": {"property": "Type", "value": "Idea"}}

The provider list ships with a default a reader carries in code and the file extends; a domain of the owner's own (owner_emails in logbook.json, policy/owner.json) is never an org. idea_rows is §4.3's, mute_days §10.5's and stale_after_days §10.6's; the status rules' thresholds of §10.4 live here too, under their own names, with the defaults the table gives. Every number is a hypothesis, as policy/stays.json's constants are.

docs.title: 5. review KIND
docs.text:
One command, one shape, five kinds:

logbook review org                       # the queue: observed orgs not yet placed, ranked
logbook review idea --json               # the queue, the unplaced and the placed count
logbook review org --accept 1,3 --reject 11
logbook review idea --name 2 "the fjord kiosk"     # accept with the owner's own name
logbook review org --all-above 50
logbook review org --status 8 hold --reason "…"    # answer a status proposal (§10.4)
logbook review place                     # = setup places review (kept, with one line saying so)
logbook review person                    # = people review (kept)
logbook review asset
logbook review                           # every kind with a queue, one block each, nothing written

7 proposals · 9 observed orgs not yet placed, 4 placed · tier 2
   1  [80]  nordmann-verft.example (Nordmann Verft, Nordmann Verft AS; mail 12, calendar 3) → Nordmann Verft AS: same domain · same name Nordmann Verft AS · Ola Nordmann on both
   2  [25]  group "nordmann verft board" (message 41) [community] → Nordmann Verft AS: same name · Ola Nordmann on both
   5  [new] fjordkiosk.example (Fjordkiosk; mail 2) → ____
   7  [new] nordmann.example (mail 30) [personal] → ____
nothing written: `review org --accept N[,N]`, `--name N "…"`, `--reject N[,N]`, or `--all-above SCORE`

The numbers are the queue's at this head and change when the record does; --json carries a stable id per pair, a digest of the two keys, and the row's hint. Every number is checked before the first line is written; a number the queue does not have, a number both accepted and rejected, or a score that is not a whole number exits 2 and writes nothing. On a terminal the command asks y, n, a name, Enter to skip or q for each proposal shown, as places review does, and writes each answer at once.

What each answer writes:

Kind --accept / --name --reject person the resolution/v1 alias lines people review writes today (RFC 0006) one entity-review/v1 line, type person (§6; RFC 0035 amendment 1) org one entity/v1 line (minting when the key is new, §3.4 rule 4), binding the domain, repo, group and merchant refs one entity-review/v1 line, type org; it MAY cite the transaction/v1 lines a merchant proposal rested on, and is then tier 3 (§8) idea one entity/v1 line binding the page, repo and title refs one entity-review/v1 line, type idea place the places.json entry, the fitted radius and the note/v1 naming line as today, and one entity/v1 line (§3.3) one entity-review/v1 line, type place, with the spot as a point ref and the name proposed, or none for a blank (§6); never again an entry in state/places-review.json alone (§6.4) asset the assets.json entry as setup assets add writes it, and one entity/v1 line one entity-review/v1 line, type asset

A rejected pair is never proposed again; retract the line and it returns. A --name on a proposal that matched a canonical entity is a relabel of nothing: it accepts the match and leaves the label; to rename an entity, logbook add an entity/v1 line that supersedes the standing one. serve's Places page answers through the same accept and reject (docs/serve.md), so its "Not a place" writes the same line.

The writers. Every write goes through Logbook.append, source manual, and nothing else writes these lines: no adapter, no import, no model, and no tool through the door (ADR 0022). Each command holds the record's writer lock from its first read of the record to its last append, as day sign does (RFC 0034 amendment 3) and as RFC 0036 amendment 1 has its writers do: it reads the head again before it appends and, when another writer moved it, is refused with HeadMoved, one sentence, exit 2, nothing written. The review reader opens no connection: no register of companies, no code host, no Notion is asked. The tests hold it to that with the network guard on.

docs.title: 6. entity-review/v1: the owner's no
docs.text: One profile carries every no the sitting writes, for every kind: the owner's statement that an observed thing is not the canonical entity a review proposed, or is not a new one. It is RFC 0035's people-review/v1 with the kind on the line, and it replaces it as the line people review --reject writes (RFC 0035 amendment 1); the people-review/v1 lines already in a record are read as entity-review/v1 lines of type person, forever.

docs.title: 6.1 Line
docs.text: kind MUST be entity-review. source MUST be manual: the owner said so. tier MUST be the highest tier of the evidence it refers to (SPEC §4): 2 in practice, 1 for a place's no, which rests on stays, and 3 when it cites a tier-3 line, as an org's no on a merchant match may cite the transactions the match rested on (§8). at is when the owner said it (for a no migrated from state/places-review.json, the entry's rejected_at, §6.4; recorded_at says when it became a line); end is null.

docs.title: 6.2 Payload
docs.text: Field Type Req Meaning schema "entity-review/v1" MUST type string MUST the kind: person, org, idea, place or asset verdict string MUST different: the observed thing is not the entity, or, when there is no entity, not a new entity of its kind (under name, for a place). No other verdict is defined; a same is the accept's line, never this ref object MUST the observed thing's strongest identifier, { kind, value }, of its kind's order (§4): a person's email, phone or name; an org's domain, repo, group or merchant; an idea's page, repo or title; a place's point (<lat>,<lon>, six decimals); an asset's mmsi, icao24, registration or subject refs array of object SHOULD the observed thing's identifiers as the lines wrote them. A reader matches a later observation against ref and every entry here observed array of string MAY the display names it was seen under entity object MUST when the proposal named a canonical entity, absent when it proposed a new one { type, id, registry }, type equal to the line's type name string MAY for a place, the name the proposal offered for the spot; absent for a blank. No other kind carries it label string SHOULD the canonical entity's label at the time, for reading the log without any table method string MAY owner evidence array of string MAY ids of the lines the observed thing was seen on logbook_head hex sha256 MAY the head the proposal was read against extra object MAY migrated_from: state/places-review.json on a no --migrate-rejects wrote

docs.title: 6.3 Rules
docs.text:
1. An entity-review line binds no ref and changes no resolution: the observed identifiers resolve as before, and every reader but the review reads as before.
  2. Against an entity. A review reader MUST NOT propose an observed thing against an entity when a standing entity-review line with that entity names the observed thing's strongest identifier, or any identifier it was seen as, in ref or refs (RFC 0035 rule 2, for every kind).
  3. As new. A standing line with no entity keeps the observed thing out of the queue's new proposals: for an org, an idea or an asset, every new proposal for that ref; for a place, the new proposal under its name, or the blank when it has none, so a spot whose blank was rejected returns when a source names it, as state/places-review.json behaved. A ref so held may still be proposed against a canonical entity.
  4. A spot is a circle. A place's point matches an observed place whose centre lies within the cluster distance of it (75 m, --radius), as the state file's rejections matched.
  5. Retraction (RFC 0003) applies: a retracted line counts for nothing, and the proposal returns.
  6. The old no. A standing people-review/v1 line (RFC 0035) is read exactly as an entity-review/v1 line with type person and the same fields. No writer writes one after RFC 0035 amendment 1; none is rewritten.
  7. Nothing requires the line. A record with none is complete, and a queue is as long as its evidence.

docs.title: 6.4 A place's no, and the state file
docs.text:
setup places review --reject has kept a place's no in state/places-review.json, which a backup leaves out; from this RFC it writes an entity-review/v1 line, type place, as every other kind's no is written. The nos already in the file become lines once:

logbook setup places review --migrate-rejects     # also: logbook review place --migrate-rejects

writes one line per entry of the file that no standing line already holds: ref { kind: "point", value: "<lat>,<lon>" } from the entry's lat and lon, name the entry's name (absent for a blank), at its rejected_at (now when it has none), extra.migrated_from the file's path, tier 1 (a place's no rests on stays), every write through Logbook.append under one hold of the writer lock. It is run once: a second run finds every entry held and writes nothing, and says so.

The file then becomes a cache. --migrate-rejects rewrites it from the standing lines, with the head it was built at, and from then on the review rebuilds it from the lines whenever the head moved or the file is missing, and reads it only to avoid reading the lines again. Deleting it brings nothing back; retracting a line does. A file without the head, the file of today, is not yet a cache: until --migrate-rejects runs, every entry in it that no line holds is still read as a no, so nothing returns before the owner migrates, it is never rewritten except by that command, and each review says how many entries are not lines yet and the command to run.

docs.title: 7. The entity page
docs.text:
logbook org NAME, logbook idea NAME, logbook people NAME (today's person page), logbook place NAME, logbook asset NAME, each [--year YYYY] [--json], and logbook entity KIND NAME for all of them. NAME is tried as a ref first (kind:value, a domain, a + number, a notion: id, an owner/name repo), then as an entity id, then as a label or alias (case aside), then as a word of a label (kiosk finds the fjord kiosk when no other idea is a kiosk); several or none is refused with exit 2 and the reason on stderr, as people NAME does.

The page has the same sections for every kind, in this order, then the kind's own:

  1. Head: the label, the refs in parentheses, the kind, the tier of the page (the highest tier of any line it rests on, SPEC §4; what the page shows past the crossing ceiling is governed by ADR 0016 as every reader is).
  2. Status line: the current status, since when (for a place or an asset, until when), who proposed it and the reason, from the last standing status/v1 line, and stale when §10.6 says so. A person has no status and the row is left out; an entity with no status line says —.
  3. Timeline of every touch: every standing line that resolves to the entity, most recent first, one row per local day (by day_start, RFC 0036) with the source, the line kind and what it was (mail from ola.nordmann@nordmann-verft.example "Q3 numbers", edited notion "Kiosk / Pricing" +340 words, stay 6 h, position 59.90,10.75 (aisstream)); under --json each row carries the line ids. The subject of a mail and the title of a page are what the line already holds; a body is never shown because it is never stored.
  4. People involved: the canonical people on the entity's lines, most days first: attendees of its meetings, senders in its group, actors on its pages, splitters on its ledger lines, speakers of its transcripts; each with how many touches and the last one. An observed person not yet placed is counted (and 3 not yet placed), never named in a row.
  5. Documents as references: the Notion pages (title, id, url), Drive files (name, id, link), repositories and mails (subject, date, the ids of the lines) that touch the entity, newest first, as references and never as copies: the record holds the title, the hash and the word count of a page, not the page.
  6. Status lines: every status/v1 line for the entity, oldest first, with its date, status, who proposed it, its reason (the note written with it, §10.5) and whether it stands; a retracted one is shown struck and said.

Then the kind's own: an org adds its domains and the ledger's net in and out by year, derived at read time from the lines its merchant refs match, within the ceiling (tier-3 lines are shown only where the page itself may show tier 3; no line of the org cites them, §8); an idea adds its title thread (the titles of its pages, tasks and transcripts, as the lines hold them, newest first), the words written by month (the sum of sync notion's word deltas), the repositories and the days since its spark; a place adds its visits, nights and hours as places review counts them and the days together there; an asset adds its last known position and the days aboard, as asset_status and the with module derive them; a person keeps every row of docs/people.md#the-person-page and adds sections 3 and 5 (a person's documents are the pages and files they acted on). A person's page shows no status, and a person draft (RFC 0036 amendment 1, open at this writing) is RFC 0036's to place on the page, not this RFC's.

docs.title: 8. Tiers
docs.text:
SPEC §4: derived data inherits the highest tier of its evidence, and a profile names the tier its producers write by default. One rule runs through the table: an entity/v1 line never cites a tier-3 line, so no name of the Manifest or the Ideas shelf is lifted to 3 and sealed with age (RFC 0029) for a transaction it was matched by; the money is derived by the page at read time, within the ceiling.

Line Tier Reasoning entity/v1, kind org 2 its evidence is mail (2), calendar (1) and group names (2). It MUST NOT cite a transaction/v1 line: a merchant match is written as a merchant ref, a folded string the ledger shows anyway, and the shelf derives the ledger's involvement at read time entity/v1, kind idea 2 its label is the owner's own words, as task/v1 and note/v1 keep them at 2; its evidence is Notion events (1), tasks (2) and transcripts (2). A transcript written at 3 is matched by its title ref and never cited, so the line stays at 2 entity/v1, kind place 1, 2 when it cites a note or a calendar entry with attendees the stays are derived from location/v1 (1); the note/v1 naming line beside it is 2 by RFC 0010 and is a separate line. The name of a home is not more identifying than the home's coordinates in every tier-1 stay entity/v1, kind asset 1 its evidence is position reports (1) and flights (1) entity-review/v1 the highest tier of its evidence: 2 in practice, 1 for a place's (stays), 3 when it cites a tier-3 line the owner's no MAY cite the transactions a merchant proposal rested on, so the record keeps why it was asked; a no is read by the review alone, so its tier hides nothing a shelf needs status/v1, kind org 3, MUST hold, add, sell and exited describe a position in money; passed and let-go are decisions (2). The envelope's tier is plain (SPEC §4), so a line at 2 among lines at 3 would say, without a key, which companies the owner passed on and which they hold. One tier for all six statuses gives that away to nobody; the cost is that the anti-portfolio seals with age like the portfolio, which is right. Which portfolio holds the company (portfolio, §10.2) is a position in money too and rides on this line, at 3, never on the org's entity/v1 line (amended 2026-10-15) status/v1, kind idea 2, MUST a decision about one's own work; the reason is the owner's words status/v1, kind place or asset 2, MUST a decision about one's own place or one's own boat. No money on the line: no price, no amount, and no transaction/v1 line cited; a sale's payment, when the record has one, is a tier-3 line of its own that the page may show beside the status within the ceiling note/v1, label status 2, MUST (RFC 0010) the owner's words on why, written with an idea's, a place's or an asset's status line that has a reason (§10.5), and never with an org's. SPEC §4 lets a producer write a higher tier only where the profile's default is a SHOULD, so the note cannot follow an org's line to 3, and at 2 it would carry an org's reason, which can name money, wherever tier 2 crosses: an org's reason stays in the reason of its tier-3 status line and nowhere else. No note/v1 line is written above 2. The note carries the words and the entity, never the disposition; the words are readable at 2, as every note is

The page's tier is the highest of its lines; an org page that shows ledger lines is 3 and crosses nothing (RFC 0005, ADR 0016). The Manifest shelf groups the orgs by their status lines, which are 3, so it is 3 with or without --money; a reader under a ceiling of 2 lists every org under no status and says how many status lines it may not show. The Ideas shelf rests on lines at 2 or below and is 2.

docs.title: 9. Dedupe keys
docs.text:
A key is what a writer looks up before minting or writing, so a second review sitting, a second machine or a re-run never writes the same thing twice (ADR 0017's rule, applied to the owner's own writes). One key per kind, folded (NFKC, lower-cased, whitespace collapsed), computed by the writer and carried under keys for readers without the table:

Kind Key, looked up through Example person email:<address>, else phone:<E.164>, else name:<words sorted> (RFC 0035's order); through resolution/v1 only email:ola.nordmann@example.org org domain:<registered domain>, else repo-org:<host>/<org>, else group:<folded name>, else merchant:<folded string>; through entity/v1 and the company resolution lines. The hint is never part of it domain:nordmann-verft.example idea page:notion:<root page id>, else repo:<host>/<owner>/<name>, else title:<words sorted, articles out>; through entity/v1 repo:github.com/nordmann-verft/kiosk place place:<name as places.json spells it, folded>; and a centre inside a named place's radius is that place already (docs/places.md#the-fitted-radius); through entity/v1 and places.json place:hytta på banken asset mmsi:<n>, else icao24:<hex, lower>, else registration:<folded, hyphens out>, else subject:<id>; through entity/v1 and assets.json mmsi:970123456

A review KIND --accept whose key resolves already reuses that id and binds the new refs to it; --name on a new key mints.

The owner's other lines:

Line Key Example entity-review/v1 (type, ref, entity id) against an entity; (type, ref) as new, and for a place (place, point, name), the blank's name absent. A place's point is one key with every point within the cluster distance of it (§6.3 rule 4). A writer that finds the key held writes nothing and says so; --migrate-rejects uses the same key, so its second run writes nothing (place, point:55.600000,4.436000, —) status/v1 (entity, status, local day), and for an org (entity, status, portfolio, local day), the portfolio folded and, on a line without the field, the one that stands (amended 2026-10-15): the writer refuses a second status equal to the standing one on the same day (the standing line's own day); a status equal to the standing one on a later day with a new reason is written (the owner reaffirmed, and said why, which is how a hold mutes a proposal, §10.5). A status that moves an org's portfolio (§10.2: to another one, case and spaces aside, or to none) is not equal to the standing one, on the same day too, and is written; one that gives the portfolio that stands, however spelled, moves nothing. A line that repeats the standing status only to move the portfolio, with no new reason, is no reaffirmation: it carries since, the day the standing status took effect, so the status's day and its stale flag (§10.6) stay where they were, and it ends a mute (§10.5), which reads the current line's reason and proposal (org 019cadd3…0201, hold, Fund I, 2026-10-12) note/v1, label status none of its own: one per idea's, place's or asset's status line that has a reason (an org's writes none, §10.5), written with it under the same hold of the lock and named by its note field

The --json of every reader carries the key beside the id.

docs.title: 10.1 Line
docs.text: kind MUST be status. source MUST be manual: a status is the owner's disposition, never the dream's. tier as §8, MUST: 3 for an org, 2 for an idea, a place or an asset. at is when the owner disposed; end is null.

docs.title: 10.2 Payload
docs.text:
Field Type Req Meaning schema "status/v1" MUST entity object MUST { type, id, registry }, type org, idea, place or asset. Never person: a person has no status. Never a goal: a goal's verdict is RFC 0036's review/v1 (§12) label string SHOULD the entity's label at the time, for reading the log without any table status string MUST one of the kind's dispositions (§10.3); any other value makes the line invalid for its kind reason string SHOULD; MUST for passed, let-go and killed the owner's words on why. The anti-portfolio is this field: a passed company keeps its thread and its reason note string MUST when reason is given, except for an org the id of the note/v1 line written with this one, carrying the same words (§10.5). An org's line has none: its reason stays on its tier-3 line, because the note's tier is fixed at 2 by RFC 0010 proposed_by string MUST dream when the owner disposed of a proposal the review showed, owner when they set it unprompted proposal object MAY what the dream proposed, when proposed_by is dream: { status, score, because: [string] }, so the record keeps the proposal even when the owner chose another status since date MAY for an org or an idea, the local day the status took effect when it is not the line's own day (an exit in June entered in October) until date MUST for a place or an asset; MUST NOT otherwise the last local day the registry entry holds: the berth given up, the boat handed over (§10.3) evidence array of string MAY ids of the lines the proposal rested on; for a place or an asset, never a tier-3 line supersedes string MAY the id of the standing status line this replaces logbook_head hex sha256 MAY the head the proposal was read against portfolio string MAY for an org; MUST NOT otherwise which portfolio holds the company, free text as the owner gives it (Fund I, Angel), its words collapsed; the empty string clears it. Absent, the portfolio stands as the last line that carried the field left it (amended 2026-10-15, below)

No field carries an amount, a price or a currency, for any kind.

The portfolio (amended 2026-10-15). Which portfolio holds a company is a position in money, like hold, add and sell, so it is a field of the org's status line, which is tier 3 for that reason (§8), and of no other kind's: a status line of an idea, a place or an asset that carries portfolio is invalid, and the writer refuses a portfolio for one, in one sentence, before anything is written. logbook status org ORG DISPOSITION --portfolio TEXT writes it, --portfolio "" writes the field empty, and the org page's status form posts the same through the same writer. An org's portfolio is the portfolio of its latest status line, in chain order, that carries the field: a retracted line counts for nothing (RFC 0003), so the one before decides again; a line a later status supersedes still counts, because a status without the field leaves the portfolio as it stood; an empty field clears it. A reader shows a portfolio, and filters by one (show orgs --portfolio, the Manifest's filter, §11), only where it may show tier 3; under a ceiling without 3 no org shows one and a filter lists no org, the same for every portfolio asked, so that nothing tells which orgs one holds.

Why not an entity/v1 line. An entity/v1 line is tier 2 and never cites a tier-3 line (§3.1, §8, decision 8), so that no org's name is lifted to 3 and sealed with age for a fact about money. A portfolio on it would break that rule one way or the other: at 3 the line would take the org's label and refs with it, which every tier-2 reader needs, and seal them; at 2 it would give the position away wherever tier 2 crosses. The status line is already the owner's tier-3 word on the position, with its writer, its lock and its form, so the portfolio rides on it: it crosses nothing that tier 3 does not, seals with the status, and adds no line and no profile.

docs.title: 10.3 Dispositions
docs.text:
For an org, six, written as these strings:

Status Meaning hold invested, and keeping the position as it is add invested, and adding to it sell invested, and reducing or looking to sell let-go the owner stopped following it, without an exit: written off, or no longer theirs to decide. reason MUST say exited the position is closed by an event: acquired, listed and sold, wound up passed the owner looked and did not invest. The anti-portfolio: the thread, the people, the documents and the reason stay, and the Manifest shelf shows it under its own heading. reason MUST say

For an idea, five:

Status Meaning spark named, nothing done exploring being written up, talked through, prototyped build being built built done and standing; the idea's page is now its record killed stopped on purpose. reason MUST say; a killed idea keeps its thread, and may spark again

For a place, one:

Status Meaning let-go the owner gave it up: a berth, a flat, an office, a cabin sold or no longer rented. reason MUST say; until is the last day it was the owner's

For an asset, two:

Status Meaning sold the owner sold it; until is the last day it was theirs. The price is not on the line let-go it stopped being the owner's without a sale: scrapped, lost, given away, a lease ended. reason MUST say

A registry entry is closed, never deleted. A place or an asset with a standing let-go or sold line stays in places.json or assets.json, and is closed from the day after until. A closed place still names the stays inside its radius, before and after until: a place given up is still where it is, and the visit to an old flat is a visit to it. A closed asset still names the lines whose subject is its id; sync ais and sync adsb ask for no position of it after until (ADR 0018: the record records what was asked for), and a position line after it that reaches the record anyway (an import, another machine's sync) is valid and shown, as ADR 0018 rule 4 has it. Retracting the status line (RFC 0003) reopens the entry. This RFC defines no disposition that reopens a closed entry otherwise; a boat bought back is for a later amendment.

There is no state machine: for an org or an idea any status may follow any, because a record keeps what the owner decided and not what a diagram allows (passed then hold is a company the owner came back to, and the two lines say so). The current status is the last standing line's; a retracted status line counts for nothing and the one before it stands; an entity with no status line has none and its shelf row says —.

docs.title: 10.4 Proposed by the dream, disposed by the owner
docs.text:
The pattern is the signed day's (RFC 0034) and the goal review's (RFC 0036): the engine proposes, the owner's answer is the line, and nothing is a line until the owner answers. The dream proposes a status when the record's own facts move, by these rules, evaluated against the head on the dream's normal cadence (each morning, with logbook dream's run, docs/dream.md) and by review whenever it runs, so the two always agree. A proposal is not a line and not a draft segment: no draft/v1 line carries it, and RFC 0036's rule that no reader derives a fact from a draft holds unchanged.

Kind The dream proposes Because org exited a transaction/v1 inflow from the org's merchant or a mail from its domain with no touch after it for 90 days, after a standing hold, add or sell org let-go no touch for 365 days under a standing hold, add or sell org passed a new org with meetings and mail in a window of 60 days, then no touch for 180, and no status line idea exploring a spark whose page or repo is touched in three or more weeks idea build an exploring idea whose repo is touched on ten or more days in a month idea killed an exploring or build idea with no touch for 180 days idea built never: only the owner knows what done is place, asset nothing only the owner knows a berth is given up or a boat sold; the owner writes it (logbook status, below)

The proposals appear in review org and review idea under their own heading after the identity proposals, numbered on, with the because-list; --status N hold --reason "…" (or the terminal's prompt) writes the line with proposed_by dream and the proposal kept; logbook status org "Nordmann Verft AS" passed --reason "…" writes one unprompted with proposed_by owner, and so do logbook status place "Hytta på banken" let-go --until 2026-09-30 --reason "…" and logbook status asset Nordlys sold --until 2026-08-31. --reject N on a status proposal writes nothing and mutes nothing: the proposal returns when the facts change. The thresholds are hypotheses in policy/entities.json (§4.6).

docs.title: 10.5 The reason, as a note
docs.text:
When a status is given a reason, by --reason or the terminal's prompt, the reason is the status/v1 line's reason, in the owner's words, for every kind. For an idea, a place or an asset the writer appends two lines under one hold of the writer lock: first one note/v1 line (RFC 0010: source manual, tier 2, text the reason as given, labels ["status"], extra.entity the entity's { type, id, registry }), then the status/v1 line, whose reason is the same words and whose note names the note. The note carries the entity and never the disposition.

An org's reason stays on its tier-3 line, with no note. RFC 0010 makes a note/v1 line tier 2 as a MUST, and SPEC §4 allows a higher tier only where the profile's default is a SHOULD, so a note cannot be written at the org line's 3; left at 2, it would carry an org's reason, which can name money, everywhere tier 2 crosses. For an org the writer appends the status/v1 line alone, its reason the words and no note field. No status writes a note/v1 above tier 2, and a status without a reason writes no note. Every reader that shows a reason (status list, the review's and the status command's output, the pages) reads it from the status line when there is no note, so an org's reason shows to the owner wherever its tier-3 line may be read, and never at 2.

The note is the owner's words in the place every reader already looks for them: the Day lists it on its day, search finds it, and the Ideas shelf reads an idea's title thread (§7) and its reasons (the status notes, oldest first) and nothing more. Notion bodies stay out of scope: sync notion keeps a page's title, hash and word count and never its text, and this RFC reads no body, Notion's or a mail's.

A hold with a reason is the standing no. No line says "never propose this". A standing status/v1 line with status hold and a reason, written in answer to a proposal (proposed_by dream) whose proposal.status was another disposition, mutes proposals of that disposition for that entity for 365 days from the line's local day (mute_days, §4.6): the owner was asked, kept the position, and said why. It is a reader's rule, documented here and settable, and no line records the mute. A hold without a reason mutes nothing; nor does one set unprompted, which answers no proposal. For an idea, which has no hold, the same rule reads a line that keeps the idea's standing status, with a reason, in answer to a proposal (an exploring kept against a proposed killed). A muted proposal returns when the days have passed and its rule still holds.

docs.title: 10.6 Dispositions as they age
docs.text:
A disposition the owner set long ago, on an entity the record has not touched since, is stale, by a reader's rule and never by a line: the standing status is a key of stale_after_days (§4.6), and neither a touch nor a status line for the entity falls within that many days of today. By default a hold is stale after three years (1095 days) and an exploring after two (730); the owner sets other statuses or other numbers in the file, and a status the setting does not name is never stale. The shelf and the page mark a stale row (stale: no touch since 2023-06-01), and --json carries stale and stale_since.

Staleness proposes nothing and does not make the dream propose more often: the rules of §10.4 run on their normal cadence. A stale entity becomes one question in the weekly dream, the dream's draft of a week (RFC 0036 draft/v1, unit week): asked once, about its standing status and its last touch ("Havn Data AS: still hold? Nothing since June 2023."), never a proposal and never a line of its own. The owner's answer is a status/v1 line, which restarts the clock, or nothing, and the shelf keeps the mark. The week's draft has no writer yet; until it has one, the stale entities are listed in review org and review idea under their own heading, and nothing asks. How the week's draft cites a status line older than the week is for its writer to settle under RFC 0036 (draft/v1 rule 6 holds a segment's evidence to the lines the unit read).

docs.title: 11. The two shelves
docs.text:
Both are readers (ADR 0013), derived at the head every run, never written, in the terminal and as pages of the Library (logbook serve, docs/serve.md).

The Manifest shelf, logbook manifest [--year YYYY] [--money] [--json], is every canonical org, grouped by its current status, under four headings in this order: holding (hold, add, sell, with the status in the row), exited, passed (the anti-portfolio) and let go, then no status. "The Manifest" is the shelf's name in the Library and nothing more: it is not a kind, and no line carries the word. Each row: the label, the status and since when, the last touch (what and when), how many people involved and the first two by days, how many documents, the reason on a passed or let-go row, in full, and stale when §10.6 says so. With --money, and only on a terminal that may show tier 3, the ledger's net in and out for the year on each row, derived at read time from the lines the org's merchant refs match. Where the shelf may show tier 3, each row says its portfolio (§10.2), and --portfolio TEXT (show orgs --portfolio, the text this shelf is implemented as; the Library's filter, /manifest?portfolio=) keeps only the orgs that portfolio holds, case and spaces aside; under a ceiling without 3 no row says one, no filter is offered, and a filter asked lists no org (amended 2026-10-15). Within a heading, most recent touch first. Nothing is ranked by amount: the shelf is a list of decisions, and the passed companies are on it as fully as the held ones.

manifest · 6 orgs · to 2026-10-12 · tier 3
holding
  Nordmann Verft AS   hold since 2024-03-02 (owner) · last touch 2026-10-09 mail · 1 person (Ola Nordmann) · 11 documents
  Havn Data AS        hold since 2023-05-10 (owner) · stale: no touch since 2023-06-01 · 1 document
passed
  Fjordkiosk AS       passed 2026-06-14 (dream proposed passed) · last touch 2026-05-02 meeting · 2 people · 1 document
                      reason: good team, but a kiosk is a place and I do not want to own places

The Ideas shelf, logbook ideas [--year YYYY] [--json], is every canonical idea, grouped by status in the order build, exploring, spark, built, killed, then no status. Each row: the label, the status and since when, the last touch, the words written this year (the Notion deltas), the repositories, the people involved, the days since its spark, the title thread's latest titles, and its reasons (the status notes, §10.5), the latest in the row and every one under --json. Within a heading, most recent touch first; a killed idea that sparked again is under its new status with its old reason one line below.

ideas · 4 · to 2026-10-12 · tier 2
exploring
  the fjord kiosk     exploring since 2026-09-20 (dream proposed) · last touch 2026-10-11 notion "Kiosk / Pricing" · +2,140 words this year · github.com/nordmann-verft/kiosk · 1 person (Ola Nordmann) · 54 days since spark
                      reason: pricing page written; talk to the ferry company first
killed
  the tide clock      killed 2026-04-02 (owner) · reason: every chartplotter already shows it

Under serve, the shelves are /manifest and /ideas, and an entity's page is /org/<id>, /idea/<id>, with the same sections as §7; the pages are rendered within the ceiling as every serve page is.

docs.title: 12. Relation to RFC 0036 and RFC 0034
docs.text:
Three things in the record look alike, an owner's word on something at a date, proposed by an engine or not and written only by the owner, and they are three, each with its own line and its own words:

Status (this RFC) Review (RFC 0036) Disposition (RFC 0034) of what an entity: an org, an idea, a place, an asset a goal (goal/v1) a commitment: a line confirmed on a signed day's page the line status/v1 review/v1 dispositions on signed-day/v1 (amendment 1), not a line of its own the words the kind's own (§10.3) advancing, stalled, done, let go, superseded kept, missed, dropped, carried its date at when the owner disposed, since when it took effect, until the last day of a place or an asset at the date the verdict is about, recorded_at when it was written the signature's tier 3 for an org, 2 otherwise 2 the signature's (1) its writer review KIND --status, logbook status (§10.4) goal review (RFC 0036 amendment 1, open at this writing) day sign (RFC 0034) what the readers do with it the shelves, the entity page the Day, the open goals promises closes a promise
  • status/v1 takes no goal. A goal is the owner's intention, not a thing in the world the record touches; its verdict is RFC 0036's review/v1, whose five words fit a goal and would not fit a company. RFC 0036 is the RFC that specifies the goal review.
  • A person has no status. A person is not held, passed or let go; what the record says about a person over time (people drift, the person page) is derived by readers, and a model's words about one are a draft, a proposal (RFC 0036 draft/v1; its amendment 1, open at this writing, adds a person unit).
  • A promise is not an entity. What became of a commitment is the signature's disposition (RFC 0034 amendment 1), on the day the owner signed, and promises reads it there.
  • One pattern. All three are one loop: a proposal, the owner's answer as a line, and the next proposal only when the record moves. review KIND is that loop for entities, and day sign for a day's commitments. If review goal joins the sitting, as RFC 0036 amendment 1 (#269) proposes, it lists goals and answers through the writer goal review uses, writing review/v1 and never status/v1.

docs.title: 13. What this RFC amends
docs.text:
• RFC 0035, by its amendment 1 (rfcs/0035-people-review-v1.md): people review --reject writes entity-review/v1, type person, from now on; readers accept people-review/v1 forever; no line is rewritten.
  • ADR 0018 rule 4, by an amendment paragraph in docs/adr/0018-assets-are-subjects.md: registry entries are never deleted, and a status/v1 line closes them with until.
  • docs/places.md changes when the reject is implemented, not in this RFC: --reject writes a line, --migrate-rejects exists, and state/places-review.json is a cache.

docs.title: 14. Examples (synthetic)
docs.text:
An org, minted at review; its domain is bound here, by the entity line's refs, and by no resolution line:

{"at":"2026-10-12T20:14:00Z","end":null,"tz":"Europe/Oslo","source":"manual","kind":"entity","tier":2,
 "payload":{"schema":"entity/v1","entity":{"type":"org","id":"019cadd3-6bc0-7dcd-9133-000000000201","registry":"logbook"},
 "label":"Nordmann Verft AS","aliases":["Nordmann Verft"],
